# Rules in force

10 decisions · built 2026-08-17 13:52

These constrain new work. A change that contradicts one of these is a defect,
not a preference — either follow it or supersede the decision explicitly.

## agents

- **ADR-0006** — In the context of a run sandbox whose skills/ directory is shared by every step, facing a later step reading a SKILL.md staged by an earlier one and answering with the wrong capability, we decided staging prunes directories not attached to the current step rather than wiping and rewriting the tree, to achieve enforced per-step skill scoping without breaking staging idempotency, accepting that the prune set is per-step and would be wrong under step-level concurrency.
  - enforced by: backend/tests/agents/test_create_runner.py
- **ADR-0007** — In the context of custom-agent artifact filenames formatted `<instance_id>.<topic>.md`, facing a small local model reading the dot as a path separator and writing `/joke/mountain.md` so the downstream step read a sentence about the file instead of the file, we decided the separator is a hyphen, to achieve a name that cannot be mistaken for a directory, accepting a one-time rename of an artifact convention that no released workflow depends on.
  - enforced by: backend/tests/agents/test_artifacts.py

## api

- **ADR-0008** — In the context of ADR-0003 making the compiled plan the run's roster, facing a composer selection of 3 agents silently executing all 9 steps the static `custom` manifest declares, we decided the roster has three ordered sources and the plan FILLS IN rather than OVERRULES — the caller's list wins whenever it has one — to achieve a runnable composed workflow that does not eat a user's agent picks, accepting that "the plan is the single source" is now "the plan is the source of last resort".
- **ADR-0010** — In the context of two competing skill-attachment surfaces — a RUN-LEVEL bag applied uniformly to every agent in a launch, and spec 012's PER-AGENT `Step.skills` — facing UI in which the same word "skills" meant two different scopes depending on which panel you opened, we decided to RETIRE run-level skill attachment entirely (UI, launch payload and save payload) and make `AgentSkillsPicker` the single authoring surface, to achieve one source of truth for "which skills does this agent get", accepting that runs with no per-agent UI (revisions, chains, wizard launches) can no longer attach skills at all, and that hooks stay run-level because no per-step hooks field exists.
  - enforced by: backend/tests/agents/test_composer_skills_delivery.py

## artifacts

- **ADR-0007** — In the context of custom-agent artifact filenames formatted `<instance_id>.<topic>.md`, facing a small local model reading the dot as a path separator and writing `/joke/mountain.md` so the downstream step read a sentence about the file instead of the file, we decided the separator is a hyphen, to achieve a name that cannot be mistaken for a directory, accepting a one-time rename of an artifact convention that no released workflow depends on.
  - enforced by: backend/tests/agents/test_artifacts.py

## engine

- **ADR-0003** — In the context of a run's agent roster being built twice — once from the compiled manifest and once from registry membership — facing a run-entry assertion that a composed workflow can never satisfy because its steps are template instances with no AGENT.md, we decided the compiled plan is the single source of the roster and the assertion is deleted rather than relaxed, to achieve one roster that composed workflows can populate, accepting the loss of a cross-file drift guard that nothing yet replaces.
  - enforced by: backend/tests/agents/test_manifest_coverage.py
- **ADR-0004** — In the context of two competing orderings — the resolver's topo-sort over agent-declared produces/consumes and the compiler's topo-sort over manifest-declared depends_on — facing four instances of one template that share one contract-free AGENT.md and therefore cannot be ordered by contracts at all, we decided declared order wins whenever the compiled plan carries a depends_on edge, to achieve a runnable composed workflow without touching the resolver, accepting that one such edge currently flips ordering for the entire plan.
- **ADR-0008** — In the context of ADR-0003 making the compiled plan the run's roster, facing a composer selection of 3 agents silently executing all 9 steps the static `custom` manifest declares, we decided the roster has three ordered sources and the plan FILLS IN rather than OVERRULES — the caller's list wins whenever it has one — to achieve a runnable composed workflow that does not eat a user's agent picks, accepting that "the plan is the single source" is now "the plan is the source of last resort".
- **ADR-0010** — In the context of two competing skill-attachment surfaces — a RUN-LEVEL bag applied uniformly to every agent in a launch, and spec 012's PER-AGENT `Step.skills` — facing UI in which the same word "skills" meant two different scopes depending on which panel you opened, we decided to RETIRE run-level skill attachment entirely (UI, launch payload and save payload) and make `AgentSkillsPicker` the single authoring surface, to achieve one source of truth for "which skills does this agent get", accepting that runs with no per-agent UI (revisions, chains, wizard launches) can no longer attach skills at all, and that hooks stay run-level because no per-step hooks field exists.
  - enforced by: backend/tests/agents/test_composer_skills_delivery.py
- **ADR-0011** — In the context of custom workflows whose steps hand files to one another, facing step prompts that name their own filenames ("save it to paragraph.md") while the engine writes and reads a machine-derived artifact name, we decided the delivery block's `artifact_name(instance_id, topic)` is AUTHORITATIVE and a filename written into a step prompt is not honoured, to achieve one filename that the artifact guarantee, the roster and the deliverable readback all agree on, accepting that a user-authored filename is silently ignored and that inter-step handoff must therefore travel through the roster rather than through names the author chose.
  - enforced by: backend/tests/agents/test_custom_agent_prompt.py, backend/tests/agents/test_artifact_fallback_and_roster.py

## factory

- **ADR-0011** — In the context of custom workflows whose steps hand files to one another, facing step prompts that name their own filenames ("save it to paragraph.md") while the engine writes and reads a machine-derived artifact name, we decided the delivery block's `artifact_name(instance_id, topic)` is AUTHORITATIVE and a filename written into a step prompt is not honoured, to achieve one filename that the artifact guarantee, the roster and the deliverable readback all agree on, accepting that a user-authored filename is silently ignored and that inter-step handoff must therefore travel through the roster rather than through names the author chose.
  - enforced by: backend/tests/agents/test_custom_agent_prompt.py, backend/tests/agents/test_artifact_fallback_and_roster.py
- **ADR-0012** — In the context of a Composer offering per-node tool grants, facing four toggles that the runtime cannot honour — two inert, one whose "off" position only disabled secret scanning, and two that made the workflow fail validation on save — we decided the grants are FIXED (`read_files` and `write_files` always on, `exec` and `spawn_subagents` always off) and no longer author- editable, to achieve a manifest that states what the runtime actually does, accepting that per-step privilege scoping is now a design question rather than a half-working feature.
  - enforced by: frontend/src/store/api/userWorkflows.test.ts

## frontend

- **ADR-0001** — In the context of SSE streams that the backend closes on purpose, facing a spurious "Reconnecting" banner on every stop, we decided that terminal frames mark the connection non-reconnecting synchronously inside the frame dispatcher, to achieve a quiet disconnect that cannot race the React render cycle, accepting that every new terminal frame type must be added to that branch by hand.
  - enforced by: frontend/src/hooks/useRunStream.test.ts
- **ADR-0010** — In the context of two competing skill-attachment surfaces — a RUN-LEVEL bag applied uniformly to every agent in a launch, and spec 012's PER-AGENT `Step.skills` — facing UI in which the same word "skills" meant two different scopes depending on which panel you opened, we decided to RETIRE run-level skill attachment entirely (UI, launch payload and save payload) and make `AgentSkillsPicker` the single authoring surface, to achieve one source of truth for "which skills does this agent get", accepting that runs with no per-agent UI (revisions, chains, wizard launches) can no longer attach skills at all, and that hooks stay run-level because no per-step hooks field exists.
  - enforced by: backend/tests/agents/test_composer_skills_delivery.py
- **ADR-0012** — In the context of a Composer offering per-node tool grants, facing four toggles that the runtime cannot honour — two inert, one whose "off" position only disabled secret scanning, and two that made the workflow fail validation on save — we decided the grants are FIXED (`read_files` and `write_files` always on, `exec` and `spawn_subagents` always off) and no longer author- editable, to achieve a manifest that states what the runtime actually does, accepting that per-step privilege scoping is now a design question rather than a half-working feature.
  - enforced by: frontend/src/store/api/userWorkflows.test.ts

## loader

- **ADR-0005** — In the context of a hand-maintained frozenset of supported pipeline types that had to be edited by hand for every new workflow, facing SC-001's rule that launchability keys on a declared flag and never on a hardcoded name list, we decided the set is derived from disk once at import and template agents mark themselves with a `template: true` flag, to achieve adding-a-workflow-is-adding-a-folder, accepting that four test-fixture manifests become visible and two ISS-015 assertions must move from "absent" to "not launchable".
